model.name: Protect history back-navigation — an EXECUTING regression gate (@390 real-device, behavioural, stub-must-fail, in gate:device:live)
model.description: History back-navigation (R40.7 historyBack + pathLabelNav on RbEditorToolbar) is a PROTECTED BEHAVIOUR and must be pinned by a MECHANISM, not a note: a regression gate that ACTUALLY EXECUTES the behaviour @390 on a real device (tap Back lands on the correct previous view; path-label nav resolves) — pixel/behavioural, never a DOM count; stub-must-fail (break historyBack -> RED); added to gate:device:live so it runs; depends on the post-deploy device-gate trigger; and NO refactor may touch the nav path without this gate green. Learned from the S23 audio player (silently regressed a whole sprint — headless-only AC, never re-ran) and the music player (died to a unification refactor that dropped an eager call nobody re-checked).
model.tronQuote: all current history back navigation is perfect... do not regress it
model.crossRefNote: Protects R40.7 (historyBack + pathLabelNav on RbEditorToolbar). Same regression class as R40.12 music-player (refactor dropped eager call) + S23 audio (headless-only AC never re-ran). DEPENDS on the post-deploy device-gate trigger (post-reset work-order top). Ties the anti-vacuity doctrine (a control that renders but does nothing passes a DOM count) + device/pixel gating.

discoverySource.note: Tron: back-nav is PERFECT, do NOT regress it. A protected-behaviour req = an EXECUTING gate, not a note. Proof this session: S23 audio silent-regression (headless-only AC) + R40.12 music-player refactor-drop. Depends on the device-gate trigger (visual gates run nowhere today = why bugs arrive as screenshots).

acceptanceCriteria.text: A REGRESSION GATE for history back-navigation (R40.7's historyBack + pathLabelNav on RbEditorToolbar) that verifies BEHAVIOUR @390 on a REAL DEVICE: tap Back LANDS on the correct previous view, and path-label nav RESOLVES. Pixel/behavioural — NEVER a DOM count (a rendered control that does nothing passes a count).
STUB-MUST-FAIL: deliberately break historyBack and the gate MUST go RED. A gate that still passes when the behaviour is broken certifies NOTHING.
ADDED TO gate:device:live (d5148b7d3) so it RUNS alongside the other device gates (it must actually execute, not just exist).

DEPENDS ON the post-deploy DEVICE-GATE TRIGGER (top of the post-reset work order — visual/device gates currently run NOWHERE, which is exactly why Tron's bugs arrive as screenshots). Until the trigger runs the gate, back-nav is unprotected.

NO REFACTOR may touch the nav path without this gate GREEN. Proof: the music player died to a unification refactor that dropped an eager call nobody re-checked; the S23 audio player silently regressed a whole sprint because its AC was headless-only and never re-ran. Back-nav meets the same fate unless an EXECUTING gate pins it.
